subject: Hosted API eval \u0014 recap, quickstart, and deployment mode questions

Subject: Hosted API eval  recap, quickstart, and deployment mode questions

Hi Samantha,

Thanks again for taking the time today  great to meet you and Tom. Quick recap from our demo and suggested next steps so we keep momentum: 

What we covered
- Demo: Hosted API endpoints (text generation + embeddings), streaming, and basic rate controls.
- Deployment modes: we talked about Hosted API (fastest to get started), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPUs, predictable throughput), and Private (VPC/on-prem for strict compliance).
- Initial ask: you mentioned a preference for a hosted eval but flagged data residency and throughput requirements.

Questions / open items
1) Data residency: can you confirm whether all PII/transactional data needs to stay in the US region, or whether a hybrid approach is acceptable for eval?
2) Rate/SLA needs: what's your expected peak RPS and required p50/p95 latency targets for the evaluation workload?
3) Timeline: are you aiming to make a decision within 234 weeks after the eval?

Next steps I propose
- Quickstart: I can send a one-click quickstart + sample prompts so your engineers can test endpoints today.
- Rate-limit guidance: we'll include our hosted rate-limit doc and recommended throttle profile for a production-ish load.
- Technical sync: loop in Marissa (solutions) and Neha (customer success) for a 30-min deep-dive if you want to validate integration points or data residency controls.

If that plan works, I'll send the quickstart package and a short checklist for the eval.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao

From: Samantha Green <samantha.green@acme-retail.com>

Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 16:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API eval  recap, quickstart, and deployment mode questions

Thanks Aditya  helpful summary. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Data residency: For this initial eval, all customer PII must remain in the US. We can anonymize product IDs, but user emails/PII should not leave US-hosted systems.
- Throughput/latency: Our baseline test will be roughly 10 TPS (tokens/sec) sustained across 5 concurrent services, with occasional spikes up to ~50 TPS for short bursts. Target p95 latency for the generation endpoint should be under 500ms.
- SLA: For the pilot we don't need an enterprise SLA, but we do want predictable throttling behavior and clear retry guidance.

If Hosted API can guarantee US-hosted processing for eval and provide reasonable rate-limit headroom, we prefer starting there. If not, we may need to look at Dedicated.

Can you also confirm the default rate limits for hosted eval keys and whether we can get a temporary bump for the pilot?

Best,
Samantha Green
Director, Platform Integrations
ACME Retail
samantha.green@acme-retail.com

From: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 17:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Hosted API eval  recap, quickstart, and deployment mode questions

Thanks Samantha  great notes. Short answers up front, then attachments and next steps.

1) Data residency: yes  Hosted API supports region-scoped keys. We can provision a US-only eval key so requests and logs are processed in our US region for the duration of your pilot. For production you'll have the option to choose Dedicated (reserved capacity in a US region) or Private (VPC).

2) Rate limits & temporary bump: default hosted eval keys are limited to 60 requests/minute and 25 concurrent connections per API key. For pilots we can request a temporary bump to accommodate your test profile (your stated spikes up to ~50 TPS). For short pilots we typically increase to a rate-limited profile that supports burst windows; Marissa will coordinate capacity/limits and suggest the right throttle policy.

3) Latency: p95 <500ms is achievable on Hosted API for most generation models at the sequence lengths you demo'd. We'll include model/sequence recommendations in the quickstart. If we see sustained spikes that push latency above your threshold, Dedicated gives predictable throughput guarantees (reserved GPU pools + autoscaling policies).

Attachments (attached to this email):
- redwood-quickstart-guide.pdf  step-by-step quickstart (API keys, sample prompts, cURL and SDK examples).
- hosted-rate-limits.csv  default limits and recommended throttle profiles for pilots.

Related links
- HubSpot demo notes: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ACME-2027-042
- Hosted quickstart doc (online): https://docs.redwood.ai/quickstart/hosted-api

Proposed next steps
- I'll provision a US-scoped eval key and send you credentials + the quickstart package by EOD.
- Marissa, can you propose a temporary throttle profile that supports Samantha's spike profile (10 TPS baseline, 50 TPS burst)?
- Samantha, if you want a 30-min technical sync this week to walk through the quickstart and region/key setup, we can do that.

Marissa & Neha  looping you in to help with rate limits and the quickstart onboarding.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
